answer: In a bonded proof-of-contribution system, every agent locks its own collateral before its output counts. A verifier traces one thread of signed attestations back to a funded identity, and clones reuse that thread, so a single slashing event punishes every alias at once. To populate a meadow of fake peers, an attacker must post one full stake per fake identity and watch all of them burn when fraud is found. That cost is the signal: identity is priced, not assumed.
